In an area model, the whole must be split into equal regions before those regions can represent fifths, eighths, or any other equal parts.
In a set model, the whole is the complete group.
The selected objects are only part of that group.
If the unselected objects disappear, you can lose the denominator.
The tick marks show where the parts start and end.
The spaces between them are the equal parts.
Count the spaces from zero to one.
You changed the model and accidentally changed the fraction too.
If the target is four sevenths, every valid model still has to represent four out of seven equal parts, objects or intervals.
A has five equal regions with two selected, so it can show 2/5.
B has six equal regions with three selected, so it can show 3/6.
A keeps all eight objects visible inside the whole-set boundary and selects three, so it shows 3/8.
B shows all nine objects in the whole group with two selected, so it shows 2/9.
The line has seven equal intervals and the point is five intervals from zero, so it shows 5/7.
The line has nine equal intervals and the point is four intervals from zero, so it shows 4/9.

A, B and C each keep two selected or travelled parts out of five equal parts.
Three of the seven objects are selected, so the set model shows 3/7.
